Hmm, morality can be tricky because it depends on cultural norms, personal relationships, and intentions. Let me think about the elements involved. Complimenting someone on an item they own might be a way to express appreciation, but does that justify expecting them to give it away? 

In many cultures, giving away family heirlooms or significant possessions can be a big deal. It's not just about the item itself but also the sentimental value. If the dad has a personal attachment to the gold watch, expecting him to give it up might be seen as taking advantage of the compliment.
